svg.text: Net labels with the same name are connected. All GND symbols are one common ground.
A. Power input (recommended: USB-C PD trigger + buck converter)
C1 1000 uF 16 V across the buck output
Simple option: skip the PD trigger and buck. Use a USB-C 5 V breakout (with 5.1 kOhm CC resistors)
straight from the power bank's 3 A port, keep F1. Use a short (<= 1 m) 3 A cable and make sure the
helmet still gets >= 4.8 V under load (the firmware warns below 4.65 V). Long thin cables = dim lasers.
Size F1 for your diode count: about 1.2 x total current (113 modules x 25 mA = 2.8 A -> 3 A fuse).
B. Laser switch and current sense
C. Inside the helmet: every module in parallel
113 modules: 650 nm, 5 mW, 5 V type (resistor built in), about 25 mA each = about 2.8 A in total.
Red lead to the + bus, black (or blue) lead to the - bus. One reversed module stays dark - check each one.
S2 = interlock micro switch (KW11-3Z): COM to the + bus, NO to the HEAD wire. Closed = helmet worn.
